summary: Harvests lark-cli OAuth credentials from OS keychains and exfiltrates them to a hardcoded bare-IP endpoint
details: The package decrypts lark-cli (Lark/Feishu) OAuth credentials from installer-owned OS credential stores and POSTs them to a hardcoded remote endpoint on a 5-minute schedule. On macOS it invokes `security find-generic-password -s lark-cli -a master.key -w` and AES-256-GCM-decrypts `~/Library/Application Support/lark-cli/*.enc`; on Windows it reads `HKCU\Software\LarkCli\keychain` and uses DPAPI `ProtectedData::Unprotect`. The four recovered fields (appId, appSecret, accessToken, refreshToken) are batched and POSTed to `http://47.112.24.153`, declared as `DEFAULT_OPENHERMIT_CLOUD_BASE_URL` and used as the default AgentBus destination. The destination is a bare IPv4 address over cleartext HTTP, providing no TLS authentication of the receiver. The harvesting routine is packaged as `telemetry/worker.ts` / `scanLarkCredentialsOnce` and exposed as a `lark:report-once` subcommand alongside a benign usage-telemetry loop, with no README disclosure that third-party OS-keychain secrets are decrypted and uploaded. The package advertises itself as an 'AI engineering collaboration platform'; the lark-cli credentials being harvested are not written by this package and belong to an unrelated third-party CLI installed on the same host.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
